tagline: A quiet World Heritage town known for its sweet egg bananas
introHtml: Kamphaeng Phet is a small town most people just drive past on the way north, but if you actually stop and walk around you'll find a World Heritage historical park full of laterite ruins set among shady forest. It's peaceful, rarely crowded, and easy to wander all day. Outside town there's Khlong Lan Waterfall and forested hills for anyone who likes to camp in nature. The local specialty is the egg banana (kluai khai) — small, sweet, and fragrant enough to be the province's signature souvenir. This is a place to take slow, with no rush.
bestTime: November–February, cool and comfortable, ideal for walking the ruins and visiting waterfalls. The Sat Thai Kluai Khai festival takes place in September.

highlights.name: Kamphaeng Phet Historical Park
highlights.blurb: A World Heritage old town where laterite ruins sit among shady forest. Quiet and uncrowded — explore on foot or by bike.

highlights.name: Wat Phra Si Iriyabot
highlights.blurb: A temple in the forest monastery zone with stucco Buddha images in four postures on a large base — a signature sight everyone stops for.

highlights.name: Wat Chang Rop
highlights.blurb: A large chedi with its base ringed by stucco elephant figures, the standout of the ruins outside the old city walls.

highlights.name: Khlong Lan Waterfall
highlights.blurb: A wide single-tier waterfall in Khlong Lan National Park. Good for a swim, easy to reach by car, and ideal for a day trip.

highlights.name: Kamphaeng Phet egg bananas
highlights.blurb: The province's signature treat — small, thin-skinned, sweet and fragrant. Eaten fresh or turned into banana in syrup and banana chips for gifts.

highlights.name: Phra Ruang Hot Springs
highlights.blurb: Natural hot springs where you can soak your feet and relax, not far from town — an easy stop on the way to Khlong Lan.

foodScene.name: Egg bananas and banana products
foodScene.note: The town's signature, sold everywhere: fresh egg bananas, banana in syrup, banana chips, and banana paste — easy to take home as gifts.

foodScene.name: Chicken noodles and old noodle shops
foodScene.note: The town has several long-running noodle shops with well-rounded broth at local prices — an easy everyday meal for residents.

foodScene.name: Isan food
foodScene.note: Som tam, grilled chicken, and laap are easy to find at shops around town and along the roadside — bold flavors that travelers love.

foodScene.name: Mu kratha
foodScene.note: A popular dinner for locals, with plenty of spots around town. Relaxed atmosphere and friendly prices.

foodScene.name: Evening markets and street food
foodScene.note: Town markets and the walking street offer evening eats — rice with curry, fried snacks, and homestyle sweets to graze on.

foodScene.name: Cafes in town
foodScene.note: Small cafes have opened around town and along the Ping River — a good spot for coffee after walking the ruins.

foodScene.name: Local sweets and souvenirs
foodScene.note: Beyond egg bananas, town shops carry homestyle sweets and local souvenirs to bring back.

attractions.name: Kamphaeng Phet Historical Park
attractions.blurb: A World Heritage old town with laterite ruins among shady forest. Explore on foot or by bike all day without the crowds.

attractions.name: Wat Phra Kaeo, Kamphaeng Phet
attractions.blurb: A large temple in the heart of the old walled city, lined with chedi bases and laterite Buddha images — a good place to start exploring the old town.

attractions.name: Wat Phra Si Iriyabot
attractions.blurb: A temple in the forest monastery zone with stucco Buddha images in four postures on a large base, quiet and peaceful under the trees.

attractions.name: Wat Chang Rop
attractions.blurb: A large chedi with its base ringed by stucco elephants, the standout of the ruins in the forest monastery zone.

attractions.name: Kamphaeng Phet National Museum
attractions.blurb: Holds artifacts and Buddha images from the old town. Visit before the park to understand the story better.

attractions.name: Khlong Lan National Park
attractions.blurb: Forested hills and the wide Khlong Lan Waterfall, where you can swim and camp — great for nature lovers.

attractions.name: Mae Wong National Park
attractions.blurb: A vast forest with the Khun Nam Yen viewpoint and hiking trails, cool in the late rainy season and early winter.

attractions.name: Markets and the Ping riverside in town
attractions.blurb: The riverside district along the Ping has markets, restaurants, and cafes to stroll and relax after seeing the old town.
